request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a crew total for the signed-in user (`my-crew-due-total`). It's the due-totals of the crews led by the person with the user's name, added up, and it stays blank otherwise. All 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

This was a front-end change only:

- **`summary/sheet-header.ts`**: added a "My crew due" entry and an input that feeds it.
- **`people/people.ts`**: added `myCrewDueTotal`. It finds "me" the same way "My due" already does: by name or alias, ignoring case and surrounding spaces. It then adds up each crew that person leads, using the same sum as the crew rows (the lead's and members' due-totals, skipping any that are n/a). It is blank when the user has no person on the sheet, or their person leads no crew.

If someone leads several crews and a person is in more than one of them, that person's due-total counts once per crew. That follows from "the crews' due-totals, added up".

I didn't touch the server or the stored data, because crews and due-totals are already loaded on the front end. No audit record was needed: this only displays a value and doesn't change anything.
